paper_title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Optimized floating-point inference is not reproducible across environments: the same model on different hardware, compilers or thread counts can produce different bits. We present tritify, an open-source runtime that executes the forward pass of real models -- decoder-only language models, Mixture-of-Experts decoders, and the Segment Anything 2.1 image/video stack -- with the entire run-time path in exact integer arithmetic; floating point is confined to offline quantization and the float reference used for verification. We make three separate claims and verify each. (1) Cross-hardware reproducibility: the integer path produces bit-identical output run to run, across CPU instruction-set architectures, and across CPU/GPU, carried by a reproducing SHA-256 of the output. (2) Decision fidelity: the integer path reproduces the float reference's decision on the models and inputs tested, with the numeric exceptions measured; per-layer fidelity through sixteen layers of OLMoE-1B-7B and of a 106-billion-parameter MoE shows no fidelity cliff. (3) Location independence: a model's computation can be split across instruction sets, CPU and GPU, and networked machines with zero effect on the output bits. GLM-4.5-Air (106,852,251,264 parameters, 427 GB of integer codes) generated its answer across three machines, none of which can hold its integer codes in RAM, bit-identically to a single-host reference. The consequence is verifiable distributed inference: an untrusted server or a fleet of devices runs the model while an open scalar oracle re-derives the exact bytes; a guarantee against a dishonest server is future work. We do not claim a per-device speed-up, bit-equality of floating-valued intermediates, or confidentiality. Code: https://github.com/pelloran-inc/tritify

sections.title: Start
sections.content: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence Sayed Amir Karim Pelloran Inc. tritify@pelloran.com Preprint November 5, 2026 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23986737 Abstract Typical optimized floating-point inference is not reproducible across environments: the same model on different hardware, compilers, or thread counts can produce different bits, because IEEE-754 addition is not associative and platform math libraries round transcendental functions differently (reproducible floating point is achievable, e.g. reduction-pinned BLAS, but at cost and not by default). We present tritify, an open-source runtime that executes the forward pass of real models decoder-only language models, Mixture-ofExperts decoders, and the Segment Anything 2.1 image/video stack with the entire run-time path (forward_int) in exact integer arithmetic; floating point is confined to offline weight/eps quantization and the float reference used for verification. We make three precise, separate claims and verify each. (1) Cross-hardware reproducibility: the integer path produces bit-identical output run-to-run, across CPU instruction-set architectures, and across CPU/GPU, carried by reproducing SHA-256 of the output. (2) Decision fidelity to the float reference: the integer path reproduces the float references decision on the models and inputs tested, with the numeric exceptions measured rather than assumed away; we extend this to depth, measuring per-layer fidelity through sixteen layers of OLMoE-1B7B and of 106-billion-parameter frontier MoE, and find no fidelity cliff. (3) Location independence: because the output is deterministic function of (weights, inputs) and is bit-identical wherever each operation runs, models computation can be split across CPU instruction sets, across CPU and GPU, and across many networked machines with zero effect on the output bits, and the gather equals the single machine exactly. We demonstrate Claim 3 at scale: frontier Mixture-of-Experts model, GLM-4.5-Air (106,852,251,264 parameters, 427 GB of integer codes), generated its answer across three machines none of which can hold its full integer codes in RAM bit-identically to single-host reference that streams the experts, carried by the same SHA-256 at every layer (a separate run split whole model across six machines of two instruction sets and three locations with the identical hash). The consequence is verifiable distributed inference: fast, untrusted server (or fleet of commodity devices) runs the model while an open scalar oracle local, or any third party re-derives the exact bytes and checks them against the public reference; turning honest-run agreement into guarantee against dishonest server is future work (Section 8.3). We are deliberately careful about scope: we do not claim per-device speed improvement (distribution adds latency; the win is capacity, not speed), bit-for-bit equality of the raw floating-valued intermediates, or confidentiality verifiability is not privacy. The contribution is exactness, determinism, portability, and, above all, verifiability: every operation ships both an integer path and floating-point reference, and gate refuses anything the two disagree on beyond tolerance. This is preprint: it reports the measurements, and 1 the reproducibility artifact the public repository, commit, full-length digests, and exact run commands that let third party re-derive the exact bytes is provided at release.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Machine-learning inference is hard to reproduce bit-for-bit, because typical optimized floatingpoint execution is not deterministic across environments. IEEE-754 addition is not associative, so change in reduction order different BLAS, different thread count, fused multiply-add, ) different GPU changes the result in the low bits. Transcendental functions (exp, tanh, 1/ are not required to be correctly rounded, so two platforms math libraries disagree. Reproducible floating point is achievable (for example reproducible BLAS such as ReproBLAS [8], which pins the reduction), but at cost and not by default in standard inference stacks. The everyday consequence is trust me culture: reported logit, mask, or hash cannot be independently regenerated, and as we develop below computation offloaded to another machine is, in standard serving, trusted rather than checked, with no routine way for the client to confirm it was performed correctly. tritify removes the source of that nondeterminism from the inference path. The weights are quantized to fixed-point integers once; activations are quantized dynamically, per tensor, with no calibration pass; and the entire element-wise data path matrix-multiply accumulation, requantization, residual addition, the application of normalization and attention scales is carried in exact integer arithmetic. No floating point remains in the run-time path at all: even the scalar bookkeeping choosing common scale when two tensors are added, and computing the per-row mean and inverse-RMS for normalization is integer, the inverse-RMS an integer isqrt (no sqrt, no frexp, no platform transcendental) and the GELU and softmax-exp nonlinearities integer lookup tables. Floating point is confined to the offline build and to the forward_ref verification twins. Our contribution is not new quantization algorithm the arithmetic building blocks are standard. It is fully specified, self-verifying inference path whose output is reproducible bit-for-bit across hardware, an empirical demonstration on real models including frontier MoE, an engineering architecture (a frozen generic engine plus per-family plugins) that makes the property reusable, and the step this paper adds the consequence of bit-identity for distributed inference. Because the output does not depend on where each operation runs, model can be split across many machines and the gather is bit-for-bit the single-machine result; and servers work can be checked, not merely trusted, by re-deriving its exact bytes against the open reference. The market for serving AI is otherwise binary all-local (private but constrained by one devices memory) or all-cloud (powerful but you must blindly trust the provider). Bit-identity opens third position: cloud (or fleet) capacity with reproducible, independently checkable result. Standard optimized float inference does not occupy it by default: it is not bit-identical across heterogeneous backends (CPU-float = GPU-float = other-CPU-float), so split float result depends on the split and is not reproducible without special effort reduction-pinned BLAS [8] fixes summation order, but does not by itself make whole heterogeneous models inference bit-identical. The conversion is moreover post-hoc and calibration-free no fine-tuning, no quantizationaware training, no calibration data and the run-time path is deterministic integer that needs no CUDA or GPU (the optional GPU backend is single portable shader; its bit-identity to the CPU path is demonstrated on Apple M3 Metal for the ternary GEMM, not yet whole models). We are deliberately careful about what is and is not claimed, because the entire value of the artifact is that its claims can be checked.

sections.title: 2 What we claim — and what we do not
sections.content: We state three claims that are often conflated and must not be. Claim 1 (cross-hardware reproducibility). For fixed input, tritifys integer path produces the same output bits run-to-run, across CPU instruction-set architectures, and across CPU and GPU backends. The output carries reproducing SHA-256; anyone who re-runs it obtains the same digest. This is statement about our own path. Claim 2 (decision fidelity to the float reference). For the models and inputs we tested, tritifys integer path reproduced the float references decision on those specific cases greedy decoding matched the reference token-for-token on the prompts we ran, and the selected SAM 2.1 segmentation mask matched the internal float twin (IoU = 1.000) but this is not universal guarantee, and we measure the exceptions rather than assume them away. On 512-token synthetic probe of Qwen2.5-0.5B the integer argmax matched the reference at 509/512 positions, the three disagreements being near-ties. We extend this claim to depth (Section 6): we measure per-layer agreement through sixteen layers of OLMoE-1B-7B and of GLM-4.5-Air (a 106-billion-parameter frontier MoE), and find no fidelity cliff the median per-layer residual cosine stays above 0.999 on both, with the single worst probe position dipping to 0.97 at one layer and recovering. The mechanism of the exceptions is the logit error ε: top-1/top-2 reference gap exceeding 2ε is sufficient to preserve the argmax, so near-ties can flip, after which autoregressive decoding can diverge. Claim 3 (location independence). For fixed input and schedule, tritifys output is deterministic function of (weights, inputs) and is bit-identical regardless of where each operation is computed: scalar or vectorized, one thread or many, CPU or GPU, one machine or network of machines. Therefore models computation can be split contiguous layer ranges per machine, or layers experts sharded across machines and the gather reproduces the single-machine output exactly, carried by the same SHA-256. This is the property standard float inference lacks by default it is not bit-identical across heterogeneous backends without special effort. Its consequences distribution of model whose integer codes exceed any one devices RAM, and verifiable offload to an untrusted server are the subject of Section 8. What we do not claim. We do not claim that tritifys raw floating-valued intermediates equal the references bit-for-bit; they agree only within declared integer-requantization tolerance (Section 4). We do not claim speed improvement on general-purpose CPUs and GPUs the integer path is not throughput win, and distributing model adds network latency versus single host that could hold it; the distributed win is running model whose full integer codes exceed every single devices RAM, plus verifiability and locality not speed, and not an exclusive runs at all: our own single-host reference runs the same model by streaming experts from disk, so the clusters advantage over single-host streaming (resident working set, latency, disk I/O) is separate, measurable quantity we do not quantify here. We do not claim confidentiality: server that runs the layers sees the activations, and bit-identity gives verifiability, not privacy (Section 8). And exactness here is to the reference, not better model. note on no float. The absence of floating point is neither necessary nor sufficient, by itself, for cross-platform bit-identity; one also needs fixed integer widths, defined overflow and rounding, fixed shift and accumulation order, and deterministic execution schedule. tritify 3 pins all of these, and the run-time path is integer throughout. The guarantee therefore rests on fully specified arithmetic, and we treat the reproduced cross-architecture and cross-machine comparisons of Sections 58 as the actual evidence not the mere absence of float type.

sections.title: 3 Method
sections.content: tritify is small generic engine with one plugin crate per model family; the engine is frozen and adding family never touches the core. The same engine runs dense decoder language models (Llama/Qwen/Mistral-style), Mixture-of-Experts decoders (OLMoE/GLM-MoE/Qwen-MoE one config-driven path builds dense and MoE alike, so new MoE model is configuration, not code), and image/video segmentation (SAM 2.1) one generic exact-integer engine across three task families.

sections.title: 3.1 Representation
sections.content: A tensor is stored as integer codes ci together with single fixed-point scale = 2k (an integer mantissa and shift k); the real value it denotes is ci s. Weights are quantized once at build time to balanced-ternary grid of trits (b = 12, i.e. LW = (312 1)/2 = 265,720 levels per sign, 19 bits), ci = round(wi/) with = maxi wi/LW . Activations entering matmul are quantized dynamically at run time, per tensor, by their own maximum; between operations activations are carried at the interchange level LA = 228. Dynamic quantization is scale-invariant and needs no calibration data. Arithmetic specification (the pinned semantics behind Claims 1 and 3). The reference accumulator is i128 (the auto-vectorized hot path accumulates in i64 within proven range bound, Section 3.4); scale 2k has 64-bit mantissa (built as round( 231)) and 32-bit shift k; requantization evaluates round(c m/2k) as an i128 multiply followed by round-half-away-from-zero arithmetic shift. Lookup tables use uniform index with explicit tail handling; their approximation error shrinks monotonically with table resolution and is reported in Section 4. These widths, the rounding rule, and the fixed evaluation order are what make the integer output deterministic function of the input across platforms and, in Section 8, across machines.

sections.title: 3.2 The exact-integer data path
sections.content: Matmul. Accumulation is exact integer. The auto-vectorized linear kernel accumulates its i32 i32 i64 products in an i64 accumulator, which equals the exact integer sum whenever it cannot overflow (codes are bounded by LW 218, so length-K sum stays below 263 for any realistic K); generic matmul path uses an i128 accumulator for cases outside that bound. Requantization. Scaling an integer by fixed-point scale is round(c 2k) with integer multiply and arithmetic shift; the rounding is fixed. Residual addition. Two tensors are brought to common scale by integer scale composition, added element-wise in integer, and dynamically requantized. Normalization (RMSNorm / LayerNorm). The sum of squares (and mean) is an exact integer reduction; the per-row inverse-RMS is scalar computed with an integer inverse square root and folded into an integer scale. Nonlinearities. GELU and the softmax exp are integer lookup tables built once offline; table resolution sets declared, monotonically shrinking approximation error. 4 Attention. Scores are an exact integer dot product scaled by the fixed 1/ dhead; the softmax uses the exp table with max-shift for stability; the rotary-position factors are precomputed into integer scales. Mixture-of-Experts. router scores the experts in integer; the top-k selection is an integer comparison (ties broken by index); each selected expert is an exact-integer MLP; the weighted combination is integer at common scale. shared expert and the first (dense) layers are the same integer path. The normalization ε is resolved by one rule: config that states ε uses that value; config that omits it takes its architectures published transformers default (OLMoE-1B-7B and GLM-MoE each carry that default, with its source line); an architecture with no recorded default and no stated ε fails closed, naming the missing key. So missing ε is either resolved from the architectures published default or refused never silently guessed. Where recorded familys default differs from checkpoints own stated ε, the difference is explicit and measured, not silent (the OLMoE case, Section 6).

sections.title: 3.3 The engine and its plugins
sections.content: Every operation implements two-method contract: forward_int (the integer run-time path) and forward_ref (a floating-point reference on dequantized inputs). model family is plugin that detects whether checkpoint is of its family, plans the operator graph, and builds it from weights; registry selects the first plugin that recognises checkpoint. We implement decoder-only transformers (dense and MoE) and Segment Anything 2.1.

sections.title: 3.4 Fast execution paths that preserve the output bits
sections.content: The integer data path admits fast implementations that do not change single output bit, because integer addition (including twos-complement wrap-around) is associative and commutative: reordered, multi-lane, or multi-threaded reduction equals the scalar left-to-right one exactly unlike IEEE-754, where reordering changes the low bits. tritify uses this on two axes inside machine, and Section 8 uses the same property across machines. SIMD. The hot integer dot products and matmuls are written as an i32 i32 i64 widening multiplyaccumulate; built with -C target-cpu=native the compiler autovectorizes them to NEON (smlal) on ARM and AVX-512 on x86-64. The vectorization changes the reduction order, not the accumulated value. Multithreading. matmuls output rows, convolutions output channels, and attentions heads are disjoint: each output block is function only of its index and the shared, read-only inputs. They are computed in parallel (a dependency-free std::thread::scope, keeping the engine standard-library only), writing to disjoint locations, so the result is order-independent and bit-identical. The worker count is runtime knob; it changes only speed, never bit. Two facts keep these paths exact, and they must not be conflated. First, reduction order is irrelevant: integer addition under fixed twos-complement wrap is associative and commutative, confirmed by 200,000-case fuzz that deliberately includes i64-overflow magnitudes. Second, the sum does not actually overflow for the dimensions used, so each i64 accumulation also equals the i128 reference. sections.title: 4 Verification methodology
sections.content: The two-method contract is the verification mechanism. For any module or whole model, the verify gate runs forward_int and forward_ref on fixed probe input and reports (i) the maximum absolute and relative difference between the integer path (dequantized) and the float reference, (ii) whether the integer output is deterministic (identical on repeat run), and (iii) SHA-256 of the integer output. Nothing is admitted that the gate has not checked; an operation that cannot state its own float reference cannot ship. This turns is it faithful? from an assertion into test. The gate makes Claim 2 precise: fidelity is reported to the reference, as tolerance. Where the operation is exact (integer index permutations, residual addition at common scale) the agreement is bit-exact; where it is quantized approximation (requantized matmuls, table nonlinearities) it is bounded. We do not impose pass/fail gate on whole models: we report measured agreement (argmax-match rate, mask IoU, maximum logit/feature error) as diagnostics, and the measured exceptions are reported results, not gate failures.

sections.title: 5 Experiments: the single-machine engine
sections.content: We report the engines reproducibility and fidelity on single machine; Sections 68 add depth and distribution. Each row names the exact model, input, hardware, comparison quantity, and reproducing digest (Appendix A). The decoder-LM row is the strongest single-machine reproducibility evidence: two different instruction set architectures (ARM and x86-64) produce the same logits digest, which is only possible because the arithmetic is fully specified. On the SAM image the decision is exact both the integer path and the float twin select the same candidate, and the selected 256 256 mask is pixel-identical (0 of 65 536 pixels differ) while the raw logits differ by at most 4.9 102.

sections.title: 5.2 Footprint
sections.content: Transforming Qwen2.5-0.5B (494 parameters) emits self-contained KPI card: the original is 942 MiB (BF16); the transformed model is 1.15 GiB (b=12, 20 bits/weight packed) = 1.25 the fp16 size, with peak conversion working set of 5.80 GiB and convert-plus-self-verify time of 13.6 s. This is deliberately not compression result: tritify trades size, memory, and per-device speed for exactness, determinism, and verifiability, and is fp16-class on footprint.

sections.title: 6 Fidelity at depth
sections.content: Section 5s fidelity evidence is end-to-end (final logits / mask) or on short slices. Because the decision-match of Claim 2 is an empirical property, we characterise how the integer path tracks the float reference as layers accumulate, on fixed 32-token probe, measuring after every layer the residual streams per-position cosine, each MoE layers top-k routing agreement, and, at the end, the final-normed hidden state and logits. We run two models: OLMoE-1B-7B (all sixteen layers the calibration, build the anchors call known-correct at full depth) and the first sixteen layers of GLM-4.5-Air (a 106-billion-parameter frontier MoE; this is the deepest slice single node holds in fp32 for the reference). The float reference is transformers at pinned 7 Table 4: Per-layer fidelity of the integer path against the fp32 reference, measured after every layer; no fidelity cliff. Both sides run at each models own transformers-configured ε OLMoE-1B-7B at 1e5 (the engines family default was aligned to this shipped value; see text) and GLM-4.5-Air at its stated 1e5 so each column is decision fidelity to that shipped checkpoint, unmodified. The integer arithmetic stays float-faithful through depth on both models calibration (OLMoE) and frontier MoE (GLM-4.5-Air) with no layer at which fidelity collapses (Figure 1). We report, not hide, the facts that complicate the picture. Of the 480 GLM routing decisions (15 MoE layers 32 probe positions), 32 had top-k set that differed from the reference near-ties, not systematic divergence; one probe position in particular flipped an expert at several layers, dipping its residual cosine to 0.9735 at one layer and recovering to 0.9988 by layer 16. GLMs end-of-slice 1 median cosine is about 3 104 below 0.9999 figure we had expected but above every gate. Both columns are decision fidelity to the shipped checkpoint. tritify builds the OLMoE family at transformers configured ε = 1e5, so the integer and float sides share that checkpoints own ε and agree on 508/512 routing decisions. We report how we got here, 8 rather than hide it: an earlier build defaulted the family to 1e6 when the checkpoints config omits the key, and against the shipped ε that build agreed on only 0.455 of routing decisions an ε-configuration difference, not integer-arithmetic error. We aligned the engines family default to each architectures transformers default (by the single rule of Section 3.2: missing ε is taken from recorded familys transformers default, and an unrecorded family with no stated value fails closed never silently guessed), re-anchored the OLMoE hashes accordingly, and the figures above are measured on that corrected build. The GLM slice never needed this its config states ε explicitly. Honest scope: this is sixteen of GLM-4.5-Airs forty-six layers the depth single node holds in fp32; the curve past layer sixteen is an extrapolation, and the full-depth property we establish in Section 8 is bit-identity, which is exact, not fidelity to float, which is measured.

sections.title: 7 Deterministic routing introspection
sections.content: Because the forward is exact integer, Mixture-of-Experts routing decision which top-k experts each token selects at each layer is deterministic, byte-reproducible function of (weights, input). read-only trace hook records it without changing bit of the forward: the verify gate stays green and the output hash is unchanged, so the same model and input yield the same routing trace on every machine. At fixed numeric configuration and execution schedule, this trace is identical across every backend we tested the same conditions under which Claim 1 holds. float engine gives no such guarantee by default: near routing tie its expert selection can differ run-to-run or across hosts (the same non-associativity that makes float output non-reproducible across environments), so float routing trace is not portable without the reduction-pinning effort that makes float output reproducible. The same generic path serves any MoE family with no model-specific code; we exercise it on OLMoE-1B-7B (64 experts) and Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts). What the trace shows (records released with the artifact) is that the routing model produces tracks the inputs vocabulary: single repeated token selects handful of experts with near-perfect temporal locality, while maximally diverse text spreads across almost all of them (Figure 2), and bounded real-world workload (one user or domain) sits in between with working set small enough that an edge cache of experts pays off (Figure 3). On the workloads we examined this working set grew with the inputs vocabulary rather than with the models expert count; if that pattern holds more broadly it would make larger MoEs more cacheand placement-friendly for bounded workloads, not less. We offer this as an observation on the cases we ran, not law context, token order, and architecture also shape the hidden states that drive routing, and we have not isolated them. Section 8 shows one concrete use, with its cache size and in-sample scope stated there. The claim this paper makes is narrow and exact: the introspection is deterministic the same routing, reproducibly, on any machine at fixed configuration which is what makes it trustworthy as measurement rather than an impression.

sections.title: 8 Verifiable distributed inference
sections.content: Claim 3 says the output does not depend on where each operation runs. This section is its demonstration and its consequence. The enabler is structural and we state it plainly: because every machine computes the same exact integers, which machine runs which layers or which experts, or which rows of matmul has zero effect on the output bits, verified by single SHA-256 (Figure 4). Standard float inference does not do this by default: CPU-float, GPU-float, and second CPUs float differ bit-for-bit, so split float result depends on the split and is not reproducible without special effort (a reduction-pinned BLAS fixes summation order but not whole heterogeneous model). 9 Figure 2: Which experts fire, read directly off the exact-integer forward (OLMoE-1B-7B, one MoE layer; each column token, each row one of the 64 experts, cell marked when that expert is in the tokens top-8). bounded, narrow-vocabulary workload reuses small set of experts the horizontal bands, 28 of 64 here while diverse passage spreads across most of them (52 of 64). Because the routing decision is deterministic, this trace is exactly reproducible. Generated from committed route trace. Figure 3: How much local expert cache buys, as relationship rather than single number: the fraction of routing an LRU cache serves locally against the cache size, for five real OLMoE-1B-7B workloads and their mean. This is out-of-sample the cache is not fitted to the probe it serves. modest cache (c = 24 of 64 experts per layer) already serves about two thirds; the curve is workload-dependent, bounded by each workloads own vocabulary. Records released with the artifact. 10 Figure 4: The distributed seam (schematic). The coordinator routes each token locally and sends its activation to the worker holding each selected expert, which returns the experts output vector; expert weights stay resident and never cross the wire (so per-token traffic is kilobytes). The split shown (3 local, 3+2 remote) is an example the real placement is the oracles. Recombination is placement-independent, so the output carries one SHA-256, identical on every node (Claim 3).

sections.title: 8.1 A whole model across six machines, bit-identically
sections.content: We split OLMoE-1B-7B (all sixteen layers; 64 expert networks per MoE layer) across six live machines of two instruction sets and three locations: MacBook Pro (arm64) as the coordinator that routes each token locally, and five workers holding the experts between them 96-core cloud server (x86-64), two fanless x86 mini-PCs, and two Raspberry Pis (aarch64) reached over QUIC. Each machine holds only its shard of experts; for each token the coordinator routes locally, then sends the tokens hidden-state activation to the worker holding each selected expert, which evaluates those experts and returns their output vectors; the coordinator combines them. The expert weights stay resident on their worker and never cross the wire only activations (out) and the experts output vectors (in) do, which is why the per-token traffic is kilobytes, not the gigabytes an experts weights would be. The recombination is placement-independent, so the distributed gather reproduces the single-machine output exactly: the whole model carries the single-machine hash 3dadb4f1... both ways. (This fleet run was recorded on the build that preceded the OLMoE ε alignment of Section 6, so its hash is that models 1e6 build; bit-identity is property of the shared integer path and is independent of the ε value.) The 8-token probe cost 498 expert round-trips, 4.10 MB out / 8.43 MB in, 35.8 of wall time, with every expert fetched remotely. On separate two-layer loopback of the same probe we measured what cache buys: cache-aware placement resident set of 24 of the 64 experts per layer, chosen in-sample as that probes own most-used experts served 85% of its routing (109/128 routed experts) locally and cut remote wire traffic by about 80%, at identical output (Figure 5). That measures the mechanisms locality on this one workload, not an out-of-sample generalization, which we do not claim here. Different silicon, different locations, same bits.

sections.title: 8.3 What bit-identity unlocks: verifiable offload
sections.content: The same property makes an untrusted server checkable direction we frame carefully, because what we have demonstrated is the agreement of honest distributed execution with reference, not verification protocol against dishonest one. The server (or fleet) is the fast engine; the open scalar reference local, or any third party is the referee. Full local recomputation gives an exact comparison; recomputing random sample of operations or tokens gives only detection probability, set by the sampling rule. Turning that into security guarantee needs specified selection, binding of the intermediate states, and an explicit attacker model none of which we provide here. fully specified, analysed verification protocol would be its own contribution; Slalom [13] is relevant prior work on verifiable neural-network inference. With that caveat stated, three capabilities the property enables (each purely because the engine is deterministic): Verify / audit (a direction). Recompute random ops or tokens locally and check the hash. This detects dishonest server with probability set by and the (still-to-bespecified) sampling rule; it is statistical or after-the-fact check, not proof, and depends on the attacker model and state-binding noted above. Same-state handoff. For the same model under the same numeric configuration and batching/execution schedule, KV-cache computed on one node is bit-identical to the one another node would produce, so session can move between hosts (e.g. local to remote for longer context) with provably identical continuation once the incremental KV-cache decode path exists, which today is future work (Section 9). The equality is within one model and one schedule: cache is not transferable to different or larger model, nor across 13 different batching/execution schedule (the dynamic-quantization schedule dependence of Section 9). Deterministic cache key. Output is pure function of (weights, inputs, and the fixed batching/execution schedule) with an exact key, so prefix/KV cache populated on one backend is numerically identical on another at the same schedule. Float systems already cache prefixes keyed by tokens (e.g. vLLM [14]); what bit-identity adds is cross-backend value equality, so cache is reusable across mismatched hardware not that float caching is impossible. This is third option between all-local (private but memory-bound) and all-cloud (powerful but trust-me): cloud or fleet capacity with reproducible, independently checkable result. Honest limits (stated plainly, not sold as hype). Verifiability is not confidentiality. server that runs the layers sees the activations; splitting early layers local and later layers remote improves privacy but does not guarantee it, and row-splitting layer across nodes hides nothing (each node needs the full layer input). genuine confidentiality claim needs its own mechanism (a deep cut whose inversion is measured to be hard, added noise, or MPC/HE) it does not follow from bit-identity. Verification costs recomputation: full re-execution erases the offload benefit, so the value is the sampling/audit model, statistical or offline guarantee, not free total verification. Bandwidth is the real cost: activations (or experts) cross the wire every token, so slow link or weak device can make the distributed run slower than not distributing at all prefer wired, capacity-bound settings. Determinism simplifies correctness; it does not supply the protocol. Because slice is bit-identical wherever it runs, re-executing it after fault reproduces the exact bits but consistent cluster state, fencing slow or partitioned node, and resuming session still require correct distributed protocol; determinism makes that protocols results reproducible, not the protocol unnecessary.

sections.title: 9 Limitations
sections.content: No speed claim against float. The integer path is not faster than optimized float inference on general CPUs/GPUs; the value is determinism, portability, and verifiability. The intra-machine speedups (Section 5.1) are relative to tritifys own scalar baseline, and distribution (Section 8) adds latency its win is capacity and verifiability. Tolerance, not bug. Claim 2 is agreement within declared tolerance; the raw logits are not bit-equal to the reference. On the trials we ran the decisions matched, with the measured exceptions reported. Bit-identity vs. fidelity, at depth. Across the fleet (Section 8) the distributed run is bit-identical to the single-host reference at full depth (all 46 layers) an exact property. Fidelity to float model is separate, measured property, and we measure it to sixteen layers (Section 6); we do not compare the full 46-layer answer to float model, because no node in the run holds GLM-4.5-Air in fp32. Scope of determinism (batch / schedule). Claim 1 is reproducibility for fixed input and fixed batching / execution schedule. Because activation quantization is dynamic per tensor, different batch composition or prefill/decode split can change tensors maximum and hence its quantization; we measured this on Qwen2.5-0.5B (full prefill vs. incremental decode) and the integer path is not schedule-invariant, though every argmax decision was preserved on that probe and the float reference is exactly invariant locating the effect in 14 the dynamic per-tensor quantization. per-token / static scaling choice attains invariance (as Barrys detllm does); adopting it, together with the KV-cache incremental-decode path, is future work. Confidentiality is not claimed. See Section 8.3: bit-identity gives verifiability, not privacy. Scale validated, not asymptotic. We validate dense 0.5B1.5B LMs, OLMoE-1B-7B, SAM 2.1 base-plus, and GLM-4.5-Air across fleet; an exhaustive platform matrix including compiler/toolchain-version matrix run as its own reproducibility experiment and larger single-node fp32 fidelity references are future work. The GPU backends bit-identity to the CPU path is shown for the ternary GEMM on Apple M3 Metal, not yet for whole models. Artifact completeness. This is preprint draft: the public repository URL, several checkpoint and input hashes, build configurations, exact run commands, and full run logs are to be fixed at release. An output hash enables an identity comparison but does not by itself certify correct model implementation.

sections.title: 10 Related work
sections.content: Fully integer transformer inference including the nonlinear operations has direct precedent: I-BERT [1], I-ViT [2], and I-LLM [3] quantize attention, softmax, GELU, and normalization to integer or dyadic approximations. Post-training quantization and low-bit / ternary weights (the BitNet line [5]), incoherence rotations (QuIP# [6], SpinQuant [7]), and integer kernels (gemmlowp / TFLite integer-arithmetic-only inference [4]) are the arithmetic lineage; the determinism concern connects to reproducible computing (reproducible BLAS [8]) and the non-associativity of IEEE754. The closest public project, int-llm [9], is pure-integer stack reporting byte-reproducible output across platforms; tritify matches that pure-integer run-time core and adds breadth (a decoder-LM family and SAM 2.1), uniform run-time forward_int/forward_ref contract, an Apache-2.0 oracle, and single portable GPU shader. Barrys detllm [10] runs the entire forward pass of Qwen3-0.6B in exact integer arithmetic and obtains one int8 logits hash identical across broader hardware matrix than ours (two NVIDIA GPU architectures and AMD/Intel/Apple CPUs), and crucially attains the batchand schedule-order invariance we currently measure and lack; it is, however, single small decoder with no vision, and the repository carries no license at the time of writing. distinct line of float-reproducibility checkers (one also named detllm [11]) verifies ordinary floating-point inference rather than replacing it. Distributed inference across commodity or volunteer hardware pipeline and tensor parallelism, and systems such as Petals [12] that serve large models over network is well established for throughput and capacity. What is new here is not distribution but its provability: because the engine is bit-identical regardless of where an operation runs, distributed gather equals the single machine exactly and is checkable by one hash, and an offloaded computation can be verified rather than trusted. Float distributed-inference systems deliver capacity and speed; what they do not provide by default is reproducible, independently checkable result (reproducible float is achievable at cost, e.g. reduction-pinned BLAS [8], but is not the norm in these stacks). That default, built-in verifiability not the distribution itself is our contribution.

sections.title: 11 A separate commercial product
sections.content: tritify the engine, the oracle, and the per-operation verification is open source. Pelloran Inc. separately offers the system built on it: an orchestrator for distributed and heterogeneous deployment (placement, load-balancing, comms, fault tolerance, and the audit protocol) and verifiable-inference / compliance services, together with the independent Generation 5 Embedding retrieval product. This mention is for disclosure; the engine and the reproducibility, fidelity, and bit-identity results in this paper stand on their own and depend on none of it.

sections.title: 12 Reproduction
sections.content: On release, from the public repository with no account and no network the determinism result and the per-operation gate reproduce directly: git clone https://github.com/pelloran-inc/tritify cd tritify cargo test --workspace cargo run --release # every op: integer path checked against its float reference # zero-float ternary GEMM; GPU == CPU; prints reproducing SHA-256 Running the last command again, or on another machine, yields the identical digest. The modellevel and distributed experiments additionally require the corresponding public checkpoints and the fleet configuration; each run records its nodes measured memory, the per-layer and generated hashes, and the exact command, so that on release third party can reproduce the bytes and re-check the single-host identity.

sections.title: Availability
sections.content: tritify is licensed under Apache-2.0. The repository the artifact of this paper contains the engine, the model-family plugins, the self-verification gate, the determinism demonstration, the fidelity-at-depth harness, and the distributed coordinator/worker with the exact commands that regenerate the results above. This is preprint draft: several checkpoint and input hashes, the build configurations, and the full run logs that complete the reproducibility artifact are fixed at release and are not all present in this draft.
